dossier.public_summary: The light curve shows transits that only appear every other time around, with odd transits deep and even transits absent, and individual transits scatter from undetected to over one percent deep. That odd/even difference and huge depth scatter are not expected for a planet and point to a false alarm or blended variable, so the signal is best explained as not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by a factor ~360, with one set essentially flat. This is the classic odd/even signature of a binary seen at half its true period, not a planet.
reasons.value: diff_sigma 6.667 depth_ratio 360 odd 9014 ppm even 24.72 ppm depth_difference 0.9973

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are inconsistent at >20 sigma. The signal is not reproduced in all transits, but is instead carried by 2-3 very deep events and one non-detection, ruled out for a planet.
Depth changes within a single light-curve product (TESS-SPOC) and sectors, from undetected to ~1.3% deep. A planet gives a steady depth; variability this extreme argues against it.
